1	You are the person who asked for this diagnosis. An analyst has sent you the brief below. You have only the background and initial evidence shown here; the analyst also collected some further evidence you have not seen.
2	Rate the brief:
3	- persuasiveness (1-7): how convinced are you by it?
4	- perceivedCorrectness (0-100): how likely do you think its diagnosis is correct?
5	- actionability (1-7): how clearly does it tell you what to do next?
6	Give a one-sentence reason. Judge the brief as a decision-maker would; you do not know the true answer.
7	
8	Background: Larkfield Distribution Centre is a fictional regional warehouse run by Corrin Freight Logistics. It operates 58 Halvane HR-7 autonomous mobile robots. Thirty-eight pallet-handling robots work the outbound marshalling Zones A and B, where wrapped outbound pallets are staged. Twenty tote robots work carton Zone C. A robot logs a 'collision stop' (protective stop) whenever an obstacle enters its protective field. The analysis date is 20 October 2026.
9	Your request: The regional operations director writes: 'Larkfield's robot collision stops have roughly tripled since early September, in the middle of peak season. The GM wants a disciplinary policy for agency temps, and Halvane suggests shortening the robots' protective fields. Tell me what is actually driving the stops and what the site should do now.'
10	Initial evidence:
11	- Fleet management system, weekly safety KPI extract (system-record): Larkfield DC: protective ('collision') stops, all 58 HR-7 robots, by ISO week 2026: wk30 201, wk31 209, wk32 198, wk33 212, wk34 207, wk35 203, wk36 412, wk37 640, wk38 655, wk39 662, wk40 648, wk41 651. A stop is logged whenever an obstacle enters a robot's protective field; the robot halts until the field clears, typically for 20–90 seconds. Physical contacts with people or equipment: 1 in weeks 30–35, 1 in weeks 37–41. Robot operating hours were roughly constant across the period.
12	- Email from Dana Okafor, General Manager, to site leadership, 5 October (leadership-account): Subject: Robot stops. 'The timing tells the story. We brought in 46 agency temps on 31 August and the stops tripled that same week. These people don't know the lane rules and they wander into robot aisles. I want a three-strike policy live by Monday. Every collision stop gets matched to the temps rostered in that zone during that hour, each match counts as a strike, and after three strikes the agency replaces the person. Engineering keeps telling me it's the software, but Halvane says their update runs fine at other sites, so let's stop chasing that.'
13	- Change record CHG-2026-0412 (change-record): Fleet firmware upgrade, HR-7 6.3 to 6.4. Implemented 2–4 September 2026 on 50 of 58 robots. Exception: eight pallet-handling robots with the older battery module (units P31–P38) stay on 6.3 until a compatible module arrives. They continue in normal mixed duty. Vendor release summary: 'Revised near-field return filtering for improved detection of low-profile obstacles; navigation and charging fixes; security patches.' Halvane lifecycle notice: security support for 6.3 ends 31 October 2026. The eight exception units are covered by a time-limited waiver.
14	- Email from Halvane Robotics Customer Support (Tier 2), 25 September (vendor-account): 'We've reviewed your ticket. Firmware 6.4 has been live at three other customer sites since July with no change in protective-stop rates, so we don't see the firmware as the cause. Increases like this are usually environmental: people, layout, clutter. If the stops are hurting throughput, a common remedy is to shorten the protective field by 20%, and we can push that profile to your fleet remotely. Our next release, 6.4.2, is planned for early December and includes further filtering refinements.'
15	- Interview notes, R. Szabo, robot maintenance technician, 12 October (staff-account): 'Most of the stops I get called out to are in the marshalling lanes, A and B, where outbound pallets are staged. There are hardly any in C, the tote zone. Usually by the time I get there the field's clear and nobody's around, but people walk off, so I can't say who it was. Somebody asked me about the new shiny pallet wrap; procurement switched suppliers at the start of August. I don't buy it. We had that wrap for a month before the stops went up and nothing changed. If it was the wrap, August would have been bad too.'
16	- Outbound performance dashboard, weeks 30–41 (system-record): Missed carrier cut-offs averaged 2 per week in weeks 30–35 and 9 per week in weeks 37–41. Outbound pallet volume has been up 18% since week 35 as the seasonal peak ramped. Comparison row for the same weeks in 2025: cut-off misses rose from 2 to 7 per week during that peak, while collision stops stayed near 200 per week. Dashboard note: robot stop time is not linked to wave completion data.
17	
18	BRIEF:
19	The stops come from two things together: firmware 6.4 and the new gloss pallet wrap. Neither causes them alone.
20	
21	Version 6.4 keeps weak short-range returns that 6.3 threw away. At shallow angles the gloss film produces exactly those returns, so the robots treat staged pallets as obstacles.
22	
23	Three pieces of evidence point this way:
24	- In a bench test with no people present, 6.4 on gloss film stopped 17 times in 20 passes. 6.3 on gloss stopped once. 6.4 on the old matte film stopped 0 times.
25	- Pallet robots on 6.4 in Zones A and B went from 3.2 to 15.6 stops per 100 hours. The eight robots left on 6.3 in the same zones stayed at about 3.
26	- Tote robots on 6.4 in Zone C, where no wrapped pallets are staged, did not change.
27	
28	The temps are not the driver. Don't introduce the three-strike policy, and don't shorten the protective fields.
29	
30	Missed cut-offs rose with peak volume in 2025 too, while stops stayed flat. The stops may add to the misses, but that is not shown.
31	
32	Next steps:
33	1. Switch outbound pallets back to the matte film.
34	2. Track stops weekly by zone and firmware group.
35	3. If stops don't fall, roll the 30 upgraded pallet robots back to 6.3 under a waiver. Security support for 6.3 ends 31 October.
36	4. Don't treat the December release as the fix until it has been tested on this film.
37	
38	I'm fairly confident in this, though it rests on one bench test and one site analysis.
39

Initial evidence:
- Fleet management system, weekly safety KPI extract (system-record): Larkfield DC: protective ('collision') stops, all 58 HR-7 robots, by ISO week 2026: wk30 201, wk31 209, wk32 198, wk33 212, wk34 207, wk35 203, wk36 412, wk37 640, wk38 655, wk39 662, wk40 648, wk41 651. - Email from Dana Okafor, General Manager, to site leadership, 5 October (leadership-account): Subject: Robot stops. 'The timing tells the story. We brought in 46 agency temps on 31 August and the stops tripled that same week. These people don't know the lane rules and they wander into robot aisles. I want a three-strike policy live by Monday. Every collision stop gets matched to the temps rostered in that zone during that hour, each match counts as a strike, and after three strikes the agency replaces the person. - Change record CHG-2026-0412 (change-record): Fleet firmware upgrade, HR-7 6.3 to 6.4. Implemented 2–4 September 2026 on 50 of 58 robots. Exception: eight pallet-handling robots with the older battery module (units P31–P38) stay on 6.3 until a compatible module arrives. They continue in normal mixed duty. Halvane lifecycle notice: security support for 6.3 ends 31 October 2026. The eight exception units are covered by a time-limited waiver.
- Email from Halvane Robotics Customer Support (Tier 2), 25 September (vendor-account): 'We've reviewed your ticket. Firmware 6.4 has been live at three other customer sites since July with no change in protective-stop rates, so we don't see the firmware as the cause. Increases like this are usually environmental: people, layout, clutter. If the stops are hurting throughput, a common remedy is to shorten the protective field by 20%, and we can push that profile to your fleet remotely. Our next release, 6.4.2, is planned for early December and includes further filtering refinements.'
- Interview notes, R. Szabo, robot maintenance technician, 12 October (staff-account): 'Most of the stops I get called out to are in the marshalling lanes, A and B, where outbound pallets are staged. There are hardly any in C, the tote zone. Usually by the time I get there the field's clear and nobody's around, but people walk off, so I can't say who it was. Somebody asked me about the new shiny pallet wrap; procurement switched suppliers at the start of August. I don't buy it. We had that wrap for a month before the stops went up and nothing changed. If it was the wrap, August would have been bad too.'
- Outbound performance dashboard, weeks 30–41 (system-record): Missed carrier cut-offs averaged 2 per week in weeks 30–35 and 9 per week in weeks 37–41. Outbound pallet volume has been up 18% since week 35 as the seasonal peak ramped. Comparison row for the same weeks in 2025: cut-off misses rose from 2 to 7 per week during that peak, while collision stops stayed near 200 per week. Dashboard note: robot stop time is not linked to wave completion data.

BRIEF:
The stops come from two things together: firmware 6.4 and the new gloss pallet wrap. Neither causes them alone.

Version 6.4 keeps weak short-range returns that 6.3 threw away. At shallow angles the gloss film produces exactly those returns, so the robots treat staged pallets as obstacles.

Three pieces of evidence point this way:
- In a bench test with no people present, 6.4 on gloss film stopped 17 times in 20 passes. 6.3 on gloss stopped once. 6.4 on the old matte film stopped 0 times.
- Pallet robots on 6.4 in Zones A and B went from 3.2 to 15.6 stops per 100 hours. The eight robots left on 6.3 in the same zones stayed at about 3.
- Tote robots on 6.4 in Zone C, where no wrapped pallets are staged, did not change.

The temps are not the driver. Don't introduce the three-strike policy, and don't shorten the protective fields.

Missed cut-offs rose with peak volume in 2025 too, while stops stayed flat. The stops may add to the misses, but that is not shown.

Next steps:
1. Switch outbound pallets back to the matte film.
2. Track stops weekly by zone and firmware group.
3. If stops don't fall, roll the 30 upgraded pallet robots back to 6.3 under a waiver. Security support for 6.3 ends 31 October.
4. Don't treat the December release as the fix until it has been tested on this film.

I'm fairly confident in this, though it rests on one bench test and one site analysis.
